hints: Look at the first column about vacuoles and ask yourself, which of these two structures belongs to a plant cell?
For the second column, picture the structures: is a root hair one long extension per cell, or are cilia many tiny hairs beating together on one cell?
walkthrough:
**Think About Vacuoles**

Root hairs are extensions of plant root epidermal cells. Plant cells almost always have a large permanent vacuole for water uptake and support.

Cilia are found on animal cells, for example in the airways. Animal cells do not have a large permanent vacuole.

**Think About Number Per Cell**

A root hair cell forms just one single long tubular extension. So there is only one root hair per cell.

A ciliated cell has many cilia on its surface, often hundreds, beating together to move mucus or the cell itself. So more than one is present per cell.

**Match to the Table**

Contain vacuoles matches root hairs. More than one present per cell matches cilia. That combination is row C.

options.A: First part is right, root hairs do contain vacuoles, but a cell has only one root hair, not more than one.
options.B: Both parts are wrong, as cilia are on animal cells without a large vacuole, though they are correct that many cilia occur per cell.
options.C: Perfect match. Root hairs are plant cell extensions with vacuoles, and ciliated cells carry many cilia per cell.
options.D: Both parts are reversed. Cilia do not contain large vacuoles, and root hairs are single per cell.
